New:

```markdown

| Control | What it does | Shown in |
|---|---|---|
| **Search...** | Filters the list as you type. In Characters mode it searches the whole library. Enter puts the first match under the cursor in the list. | every mode |
| **New** | Creates a new item in the current mode. ("Create a new item in this mode.") | every mode |
| **Import** | Opens a file picker; the tooltip names the accepted formats per mode — "Import a character card (PNG or JSON).", "Import a dictionary (JSON or Markdown).", "Import a world book (JSON)." | Characters, Dictionaries, Lore — **hidden in Personas** |
| **Duplicate** | Copies the selected item. ("Duplicate the selected item.") | Characters, Dictionaries, Lore — **hidden in Personas** |
| **Sort: Name** | Cycles the list order — Name → Recent edit → Recent add (plus Relevance while a Characters search is running). ("Cycle the list sort order.") | Characters, Personas — **hidden in Dictionaries and Lore** |
| **Tag: All** | Opens the "Filter by tag" picker. ("Filter characters by tag.") | **Characters only** |

**Empty states** name the way out: "No characters yet - use New or
Import to add one.", "No personas yet - use New to add one." (Personas has
no Import), and the same "use New or Import" wording for "No dictionaries
yet - …" and "No lore books yet - …".

#### The list

Every item takes one line when the list is narrow (as at 120 columns) or a
kind holds more than 40 items. When the list is at least 40 cells wide and
the kind holds 40 or fewer, each item takes two lines, the second one dim:
a character's age, first tag and the start of its description ("3d ·
fantasy · Commands the…"), the first words of a persona's system prompt,
"250 entries" for a lore book, "150 rules" for a dictionary. Lore books and
dictionaries end their first line with **on** or **off**, and a book that
is off has a muted name. A name too long for the list is cut in the middle
("Highspire Gazette…om card) 2"); hover over it to read it whole.

The first columns are a gutter: **▸** marks the item open in the centre
pane and **✓** a marked item (">" and "[x]" with ASCII glyphs on).

There are no pages. The list scrolls through the whole library and loads
200 more rows as you near the end; **End** jumps to the last item and loads
the rest on the way. Personas lists every persona, not only the newest 100.

Highlighting a row doesn't open it: press **Enter** or click. With the list
focused, **Space** turns the highlighted lore book or dictionary on or off
(turning one off says "{name} turned off · space to undo"; press **Space**
again to undo), and **s** cycles the sort in Characters and Personas. These
keys act on the list only, never on a focused button.

#### Counts in the border

The list's top border names the kind and its count: "Characters 349",
"Personas 114", "Lore books 3 · 2 on" and "Chat dictionaries 3 · 2 on"
(books add how many are on). While a search or a tag narrows the list it
reads "Characters 48 of 349", adding "· tag fantasy" for a tag. It shows
"(…)" while counting, "100+" on a server until the total is known, and
"(?)" when the list could not load.

The bottom border gives the open item's place in the list, "#4 of 28". It
is blank while nothing is open, or while a search hides the open item.

#### Marks and the marks bar

To act on several items at once, mark them: press **m** on the highlighted
row, or click its ✓ column (the tooltip reads "Click to mark"). Do the same
again to unmark. A click anywhere else on a row opens the item and never
marks it.

While marks exist, the list's bottom row is the **marks bar**:
"✓ 3 marked · Export… · Delete… · Clear esc". Lore books and dictionaries
have no **Export…**. On a narrow list the bar drops words but keeps the
count and its buttons.

Marks are kept per kind. They survive searching, sorting, tags and
switching to another kind and back. When a search or tag hides some of
them, the bar says so: "✓ 3 marked (2 hidden)". **Clear** (or **Escape**)
clears the current kind's marks. Leaving Roleplay clears them all: marks
are never saved.

- **Export…** asks for a folder ("Export 3 items as JSON") and writes one
  JSON file per marked item.
- **Delete…** opens the delete dialog below, naming the marked items.

The Inspector's **Export JSON** and **Delete** act on the open item only,
whatever is marked.

#### Deleting

Every delete asks once, in the same dialog:

- The Inspector's **Delete** asks "Delete {name}? This cannot be undone
  here." (**Delete** / **Cancel**).
- The marks bar's **Delete…** is titled "Delete 3 marked" and asks "Delete
  these 3 characters? This cannot be undone here.", then lists up to five
  names and "and N more". Its confirm button reads **Delete 3 marked**.

**Cancel** has the focus, and **Escape** cancels. Focus then returns to the
button you pressed.

### The Inspector
```

Spec §5.4 item 4 (the PS row and a recipient-ceiling row for code moved out of a governed module), §5.10 (`PS` lines row: new recipient rows, `personas_library_pane.py` among them), R-131; owner ruling 1 of 2026-10-19: "Expand limits, never contort code" (Global Constraints). Task 2 already set `roleplay_frame_state.py`'s recipient row to its measurement (384 → 920) and Task 5 raised it with C1's ladder (920 → 928); Task 9 already lowered the broad-selector ratchet (274 → 269). This task holds the two rows and the one derived file the gates step found. Raising the PS row here, once, is the ruling recorded in Global Constraints (plan review, 2026-10-21): that row was red on dev before B2a, the owner's words ("just expand the limits, don't modify other modules to make this fit") ask for the raise and not for a raise per commit, and the PR merges as one; Tasks 3-11 leave the already-red row red.

- **`personas_screen.py` (PS):** its row is red on dev today, and B2a does not cause that: B1 set the row to 16,564 on 2026-10-09, then dev grew the file to 16,617 (`57ef384caf` +4, `66a940d1a7` +22, `fad849155b` +27), so `test_module_size_ratchet.py` fails for PS on the base arm. The ratchet only accepts a row at or above the line count, so the row rises to 16,833, which absorbs dev's +53 as well as B2a's +216; the dated owner-decision comment names the three dev commits. As a side effect B2a turns that dev-red row green. ```bash

"""B2a gates: every _BUDGETS row in test_module_size_ratchet.py vs its measured lines; marks rows for files the branch touches."""
import ast, sys
from pathlib import Path
root = Path(sys.argv[1]); touched = set(Path(sys.argv[2]).read_text().split())
src = (root / "Tests/Architecture/test_module_size_ratchet.py").read_text()
tree = ast.parse(src)
budgets = None
for node in ast.walk(tree):
    if isinstance(node, (ast.Assign, ast.AnnAssign)):
        tgt = node.targets[0] if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) else node.target
        if getattr(tgt, "id", None) == "_BUDGETS":
            budgets = ast.literal_eval(node.value)
for rel, row in budgets.items():
    p = root / rel
    lines = len(p.read_text().splitlines()) if p.exists() else -1
    state = "OK" if row - 50 <= lines <= row else ("GROWN" if lines > row else "SLACK")
    mark = "TOUCHED" if rel in touched else ""
    if state != "OK" or mark:
        print(f"{state:5} {mark:7} {rel}: lines {lines} row {row} (delta {lines-row:+d})")
EOF
git -C "$WT" diff --name-only "$(cat "$EV/base-sha.txt")"...HEAD > "$GD/touched.txt"
(cd "$WT" && "$PY" "$EV/ratchet_rows.py" | sed 's/^/ratchet rows: /') | tee -a "$GD/gates.txt"
for ARM in base head; do
  if [ "$ARM" = base ]; then T=$BASE; else T=$WT; fi
  "$PY" "$GD/ratchet_report.py" "$T" "$GD/touched.txt" | sed "s/^/ratchet $ARM: /" | tee -a "$GD/gates.txt"
  (cd "$T" && "$PY" -m pytest Tests/Architecture/test_module_size_ratchet.py -p no:cacheprovider -q 2>&1 | grep -E '[0-9]+ (passed|failed|error)' | tail -1 | sed "s/^/ratchet $ARM test: /") | tee -a "$GD/gates.txt"
done
OUTER
```

# ruff_compare.sh: for every .py file the branch changed (base...HEAD), the ruff check findings and
# the ruff format state on the base arm and on head; one row per file, then one verdict line.
# head is "worse" when it has more findings than base, or more formatter hunks than base (a new
# file counts as zero on base).
set -u

WT=${HEAD_WT:-$MAIN/.worktrees/roleplay-b2a}; BASE=${BASE_WT:-$MAIN/.worktrees/roleplay-b2a-base}

worse=0; n=0
state() { # state <worktree> <file> -> "<findings> <hunks>" or "absent"
  if [ ! -f "$1/$2" ]; then echo absent; return; fi
  local c h
  c=$(cd "$1" && "$RUFF" check --output-format concise "$2" 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '^[^ ]+:[0-9]+:[0-9]+: ')
  h=$(cd "$1" && "$RUFF" format --diff "$2" 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^@@')
  echo "$c $h"
}
for f in $(git -C "$WT" diff --name-only "$B"...HEAD -- '*.py'); do
  n=$((n + 1))
  b=$(state "$BASE" "$f"); h=$(state "$WT" "$f")
  verdict=ok
  if [ "$h" != absent ]; then
    set -- $h; hc=$1; hh=$2
    if [ "$b" = absent ]; then bc=0; bh=0; else set -- $b; bc=$1; bh=$2; fi
    if [ "$hc" -gt "$bc" ] || [ "$hh" -gt "$bh" ]; then verdict=WORSE; worse=$((worse + 1)); fi
  fi
  printf '%-74s base=%-9s head=%-9s %s\n' "$f" "${b// //}" "${h// //}" "$verdict"
done
echo "ruff: $n changed .py files, head worse than base in $worse (findings/formatter hunks per arm above)"
EOF

B2a retires the ListView path and adds a window worker, so the capture is required. Same key script on both arms on a real `TldwCli` at 120x36 over a file-backed ChaChaNotes with 348 seeded characters: arrive; Ctrl+F `Character 01`; Backspace ×12; Escape and End; resize 120 → 160 → 120; `l` then `c`; Ctrl+1 then Ctrl+4; idle 2 s. It records the heartbeat (a 5 ms sleeper's longest gap and the gaps over 250 ms), the app monitor's snapshot, the worker backlog (peak and final live workers), the timer registry (live timers at start and end) and mount churn (widgets mounted and removed, per phase). The capture is a test module copied, untracked, into an arm's `Tests/UI/`, so the arm's conftest isolates config and data; the base arm's copy runs in a scratch worktree at the base SHA, removed after, so the paired base arm itself is never written. ```bash
bash <<'OUTER'
set -u

cat > "$A/test_zz_adr011_capture.py" <<'EOF'
"""B2a ADR-011 before/after capture (evidence only; never committed).

Copied into an arm's Tests/UI/ as an untracked file and run there with the
bootstrap plugin, so the arm's conftest isolates config and data. Same key
script on both arms (keys only, no arm-specific API): arrive at Roleplay on a
real TldwCli over a file-backed ChaChaNotes holding 348 seeded characters,
search, clear, End, resize 120->160->120, kind switch, leave and return, idle.

Records (ADR-011: heartbeat, worker backlog, timer registry, mount churn):
the event loop's longest gap (a 5 ms sleeper), the app monitor's own snapshot,
peak and final live workers, live timers at start and end, widgets mounted and
removed during the script, and the Roleplay screen's widget count.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import os
import time
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

import pytest
from textual.app import App
from textual.worker import WorkerState

import tldw_chatbook.app  # noqa: F401
import tldw_chatbook.config as config_module
from Tests.app_module_patches import patch_app_global
from Tests.UI.app_factory import _build_test_app
from tldw_chatbook.DB.ChaChaNotes_DB import CharactersRAGDB

pytestmark = [pytest.mark.bootstrap_profile, pytest.mark.asyncio]

OUT = Path(os.environ["ADR011_OUT"])
COUNT = 348


def _settings(section, key=None, default=None):
    if section == "splash_screen" and key == "enabled":
        return False
    return default


def _live_workers(app) -> int:
    return sum(
        1
        for worker in app.workers
        if worker.state in (WorkerState.PENDING, WorkerState.RUNNING)
    )


def _live_timers(app) -> int:
    nodes = [app, *app.screen_stack, *list(app._registry)]
    seen = set()
    live = 0
    for node in nodes:
        for timer in list(getattr(node, "_timers", ())):
            if id(timer) in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(id(timer))
            task = getattr(timer, "_task", None)
            if task is not None and not task.done():
                live += 1
    return live


async def _wait(pilot, predicate, timeout=30.0):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        if predicate():
            return
        await pilot.pause(0.02)
    raise AssertionError("timed out")


async def _settle(pilot):
    await pilot.pause()
    screen = pilot.app.screen
    for _ in range(500):
        busy = [
            w
            for w in pilot.app.workers
            if w.node is screen
            and w.state in (WorkerState.PENDING, WorkerState.RUNNING)
        ]
        if not busy:
            break
        await pilot.pause(0.02)
    await pilot.pause()
    await pilot.pause()


async def test_adr011_capture(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    db = CharactersRAGDB(tmp_path / "chachanotes.db", "b2a-adr011")
    with db.transaction():
        for index in range(COUNT):
            name = "Captain Isolde Varga" if index == 0 else f"Character {index:04d}"
            db.add_character_card(
                {
                    "name": name,
                    "description": f"Seeded volume character number {index}.",
                    "tags": [("fantasy", "sci-fi", "noir")[index % 3]],
                }
            )
    tally = {"mounted": 0, "armed": False}
    register = App._register

    def counted_register(self, parent, *widgets, **kwargs):
        if tally["armed"]:
            tally["mounted"] += len(widgets)
        return register(self, parent, *widgets, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(App, "_register", counted_register)
    app = _build_test_app(configured_default="personas")
    phases: dict[str, dict] = {}
    try:
        with (
            patch_app_global("get_cli_setting", side_effect=_settings),
            patch.object(config_module, "get_chachanotes_db_lazy", lambda: db),
        ):
            async with app.run_test(size=(120, 36)) as pilot:
                await _wait(
                    pilot,
                    lambda: type(app.screen).__name__ == "PersonasScreen"
                    and getattr(app.screen, "_character_total", None) == COUNT + 1,
                )
                await _settle(pilot)
                screen = app.screen
                widgets_at_arrival = len(list(screen.query("*")))
                timers_start = _live_timers(app)
                gaps: list[float] = []
                peak = {"workers": _live_workers(app)}
                running = True

                async def heartbeat():
                    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
                    previous = loop.time()
                    while running:
                        await asyncio.sleep(0.005)
                        now = loop.time()
                        gaps.append(now - previous)
                        previous = now
                        peak["workers"] = max(peak["workers"], _live_workers(app))

                beat = asyncio.create_task(heartbeat())
                tally["armed"] = True
                nodes_start = len(app._registry)

                async def phase(name, coro):
                    start_gap, start_m = len(gaps), tally["mounted"]
                    start_nodes = len(app._registry)
                    began = time.perf_counter()
                    await coro
                    await _settle(pilot)
                    window = gaps[start_gap:] or [0.0]
                    mounted = tally["mounted"] - start_m
                    phases[name] = {
                        "max_gap_ms": round(max(window) * 1000, 1),
                        "mounted": mounted,
                        # live nodes: removed = mounted - net growth
                        "removed": mounted - (len(app._registry) - start_nodes),
                        "wall_ms": round((time.perf_counter() - began) * 1000, 1),
                    }

                async def search():
                    await pilot.press("ctrl+f", *"Character 01")
                    await asyncio.sleep(0.4)

                async def clear():
                    await pilot.press(*(["backspace"] * len("Character 01")))
                    await asyncio.sleep(0.4)

                async def end():
                    await pilot.press("escape", "end")
                    await asyncio.sleep(0.4)

                async def resize():
                    await pilot.resize_terminal(160, 45)
                    await _settle(pilot)
                    await pilot.resize_terminal(120, 36)

                async def kinds():
                    await pilot.press("l")
                    await _settle(pilot)
                    await pilot.press("c")

                async def leave_return():
                    await pilot.press("ctrl+1")
                    await _wait(pilot, lambda: type(app.screen).__name__ != "PersonasScreen")
                    await _settle(pilot)
                    await pilot.press("ctrl+4")
                    await _wait(
                        pilot,
                        lambda: type(app.screen).__name__ == "PersonasScreen"
                        and getattr(app.screen, "_character_total", None) == COUNT + 1,
                    )

                await phase("search", search())
                await phase("clear", clear())
                await phase("end", end())
                await phase("resize", resize())
                await phase("kinds", kinds())
                await phase("leave_return", leave_return())
                await asyncio.sleep(2.0)
                tally["armed"] = False
                running = False
                await beat
                snap = app.ui_responsiveness_monitor.snapshot()
                result = {
                    "head": os.environ.get("ADR011_ARM", "?"),
                    "widgets_at_arrival": widgets_at_arrival,
                    "widgets_at_end": len(list(app.screen.query("*"))),
                    "max_loop_gap_ms": round(max(gaps) * 1000, 1),
                    "loop_gaps_over_250ms": sum(1 for g in gaps if g > 0.25),
                    "peak_live_workers": peak["workers"],
                    "live_workers_at_end": _live_workers(app),
                    "live_timers_start": timers_start,
                    "live_timers_end": _live_timers(app),
                    "mounted_total": tally["mounted"],
                    "removed_total": tally["mounted"] - (len(app._registry) - nodes_start),
                    "monitor": {
                        "max_heartbeat_lag_ms": snap.max_heartbeat_lag_ms,
                        "stalled": snap.stalled,
                        "active_workers": snap.active_workers,
                        "active_timers": snap.active_timers,
                    },
                    "phases": phases,
                }
                OUT.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    finally:
        db.close_connection()
EOF
cat > "$A/run_adr011.sh" <<'EOF'

esac
cp "$A/test_zz_adr011_capture.py" "$T/Tests/UI/test_zz_adr011_capture.py"
(cd "$T" && ADR011_OUT="$A/adr011-$1-$2.json" ADR011_ARM="$1" PYTHONPATH="$EV/plug:$T" "$PY" -m pytest Tests/UI/test_zz_adr011_capture.py \
  -p b1_bootstrap_all -p no:cacheprovider -q --basetemp="$A/bt-adr011-$1-$2" > "$A/adr011-$1-$2.log" 2>&1)
echo "adr011 run $1 $2: $(grep -E '[0-9]+ (passed|failed|error)' "$A/adr011-$1-$2.log" | tail -1)"

Usage: adr011_summary.py <dir holding adr011-<arm>-<n>.json>

)


def cell(values) -> str:

print(f"adr011 runs: base {len(runs['base'])}, head {len(runs['head'])}")
print(f"adr011 {'metric':<27}{'base':>28}{'head':>28}")
for metric in METRICS:
    print(f"adr011 {metric:<27}{cell([r[metric] for r in runs['base']]):>28}{cell([r[metric] for r in runs['head']]):>28}")
for key in ("max_heartbeat_lag_ms", "stalled", "active_workers", "active_timers"):
    base = " ".join(str(r["monitor"][key]) for r in runs["base"])
    head = " ".join(str(r["monitor"][key]) for r in runs["head"])

        parts.append(f"{arm} {gap:7.1f} / {mounted:5g} / {removed:5g}")
    print(f"adr011   {phase:<13}" + "    ".join(parts))
EOF

- [ ] **Step 7: Live-harness evidence for AC#9 and AC#10 (evidence, never a pytest threshold)**

AC#9 asks for "the median of at least 10 ABBA-interleaved runs at 348 and 5,000 characters, from key event to first idle after paint", recorded in the §5.10 ledger against ≤250 ms, with `set_options` ≤50 ms at 348; AC#10 asks for recorded live evidence that a 120 ↔ 160 resize and End settle within the same budget with every row resident. The harness supplies the real terminal (`App._display` writes nothing when headless, which is why this cannot be Pilot); the timing comes from inside the app. Isolation, every launch: the harness's `env -i` allow-list gives the app a disposable `HOME`, both XDG path families (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, plus `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and `XDG_STATE_HOME`), `TLDW_CONFIG_PATH` inside the run and `PYTHON_KEYRING_BACKEND=keyring.backends.null.Keyring`, with no inherited provider keys; seeding goes only through `seedrun.sh`, which runs the same isolation and `harness_guard.py`'s REFUSING checks; `HARNESS_STATE` is B2a-private (`$EV/harness-state`) so no other session can rebuild or overwrite the masters mid-run; `launch.sh --self-test` proves the real profile and the login keychain are unchanged.

What is measured, per event (`$EV/live/inject/sitecustomize.py`, loaded through the harness's `EXTRA_PYTHONPATH` on both arms alike): from the key or resize event's arrival at the app (`time.perf_counter`) to the first idle after the paint that shows its result: the last list update the event caused (`PersonasLibraryPane.update_rows` on both arms, `RoleplayItemList.append_rows` and the list's `set_options` on head) or the end of the last screen worker it started, then a real terminal write, then the first moment the screen has processed its queue with nothing dirty, no after-refresh callback, no message queued or being handled on the app, the screen or its widgets, no screen worker pending or running and no one-shot timer pending on the screen (the 0.2 s search debounce among them). A search keystroke therefore includes the 0.2 s debounce (`PERSONAS_SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS`, unchanged from dev): its budget for the count, the window, `set_options` and the paint is about 50 ms. The hooks change no behaviour (each calls the original and swallows its own errors); writing them took four rounds, each found by a smoke run, recorded here because the next writer will meet the same traps: Textual's paint runs in the screen's update-timer task, so no Idle follows it by itself (the hook posts a `call_later` from the paint); a debounce timer's callback is queued with `call_next`, outside the message queue; Textual's message queue has no unfinished-task count, so a node still handling a key looks idle unless dispatch is counted; and `App.screen` is the current screen, so an app-level worker looks like a screen worker unless the App is excluded.

Each run is one cold launch at 120x36 on a copy of the profile, then: Ctrl+F; `a`, `l` (two debounced search keystrokes); Backspace ×2; Escape (into the list); Down ×3; End (at 5,000 a load-through of every window); Home; End again (every row resident: AC#10's End); resize to 160x45 and back to 120x36 (AC#10's resize). Ten runs per arm per profile, ABBA-interleaved (base head head base, five times), 348 characters (`volume`) then 5,000 (`volume5000`, the harness's `volume` topped up through the app's own API; spec §5.7.5 asks `make_profiles.sh` for that copy, which dev's harness lacks, so this step builds it).

"""B2a live timing (AC#9, AC#10): evidence only, never committed.

Loaded through the harness's EXTRA_PYTHONPATH, so it runs inside the real app
in tmux on both arms with the same hooks. For every key event and every

records the milliseconds from the event's arrival (``time.perf_counter``) to
the first idle after the paint that shows the event's result:

* "result" = the last list update the event caused (``PersonasLibraryPane.
  update_rows``, ``RoleplayItemList.append_rows``, the list's ``set_options``)
  or the end of the last worker it started on the screen; with none, the
  event itself;
* "paint" = a real write to the terminal (``App._display``; a no-op when
  headless, which is why this is the live harness and never Pilot);
* "idle" = the first moment after that paint when the screen has processed
  its queue (a ``call_later`` posted by the paint, or ``Screen._on_idle``)
  with nothing dirty, no after-refresh callback pending, no message queued on
  the app, the screen or any of its widgets, no worker of the screen pending
  or running and no one-shot timer pending anywhere on the screen (the 0.2 s
  search debounce among them).

It also records how long each ``set_options`` on ``#personas-library-rows``
took (head only: the base arm's list is a ListView). One JSON line per event
goes to ``$HOME/b2a-timing.jsonl`` (HOME is the harness run's own home);
``why`` counts the checks that found the screen not yet settled. It changes
no behaviour: every hook calls the original and swallows its own errors.
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import time

_OUT = os.path.join(os.environ.get("HOME", "."), "b2a-timing.jsonl")
_PENDING: dict | None = None
_PANE_PATCHED = False
#: Messages each node is handling right now, by id(node) (Textual's queue has no unfinished count).
_IN_FLIGHT: dict[int, int] = {}


def _emit(record: dict) -> None:
    try:
        with open(_OUT, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
    except Exception:
        pass


def _report(pending: dict, now: float) -> dict:
    t0 = pending["t0"]
    return {
        "label": pending["label"],
        "ms": round((now - t0) * 1000, 2),
        "work_ms": round((pending["t_work"] - t0) * 1000, 2),
        "paints": pending["paints"],
        "set_options_ms": pending["set_options_ms"],
        "why": pending["why"],
    }


def _start(label: str) -> None:
    global _PENDING
    now = time.perf_counter()
    if _PENDING is not None:
        _emit({**_report(_PENDING, now), "status": "superseded"})
    _PENDING = {
        "label": label,
        "t0": now,
        "t_work": now,
        "t_paint": 0.0,
        "paints": 0,
        "set_options_ms": [],
        "why": {},
    }


def _work_done() -> None:
    if _PENDING is not None:
        _PENDING["t_work"] = time.perf_counter()


def _owned_by(node, screen) -> bool:
    """True for the screen and its widgets (never the App, whose .screen is the current screen)."""
    from textual.app import App

    return node is screen or (not isinstance(node, App) and getattr(node, "screen", None) is screen)


def _patch_pane() -> None:
    """Wrap the list's update points once the Roleplay modules are loaded (lazily, never at boot)."""
    global _PANE_PATCHED
    module = sys.modules.get("tldw_chatbook.Widgets.Persona_Widgets.personas_library_pane")
    if _PANE_PATCHED or module is None:
        return
    _PANE_PATCHED = True
    pane_cls = module.PersonasLibraryPane
    original_update = pane_cls.update_rows

    async def update_rows(self, *args, **kwargs):
        try:
            return await original_update(self, *args, **kwargs)
        finally:
            _work_done()

    pane_cls.update_rows = update_rows
    item_list_cls = getattr(module, "RoleplayItemList", None)
    if item_list_cls is not None and hasattr(item_list_cls, "append_rows"):
        original_append = item_list_cls.append_rows

        def append_rows(self, *args, **kwargs):
            try:
                return original_append(self, *args, **kwargs)
            finally:
                _work_done()

        item_list_cls.append_rows = append_rows


def _not_settled(screen, own: int = 0) -> str:
    """Why the screen is not settled yet, or "" when it is.

    ``own`` is 1 when the check itself runs as a message of the screen (a
    ``call_later``), which the screen's unfinished-message count then includes.
    """
    from textual.worker import WorkerState

    if (
        screen._layout_required
        or screen._scroll_required
        or screen._repaint_required
        or screen._recompose_required
        or screen._dirty_widgets
        or screen._callbacks
    ):
        return "dirty"
    nodes = (screen, *screen.walk_children())
    for node in (screen.app, *nodes):
        handling = _IN_FLIGHT.get(id(node), 0) - (own if node is screen else 0)
        if handling > 0 or not node._message_queue.empty() or node._next_callbacks:
            return f"queued:{type(node).__name__}"
    for worker in list(screen.app.workers):
        if worker.state in (WorkerState.PENDING, WorkerState.RUNNING) and _owned_by(worker.node, screen):
            return f"worker:{worker.group}:{worker.name}"
    for node in nodes:
        for timer in list(getattr(node, "_timers", ())):
            task = getattr(timer, "_task", None)
            if getattr(timer, "_repeat", None) == 0 and task is not None and not task.done():
                return f"timer:{type(node).__name__}:{timer.name}"
    return ""


def _check(screen, own: int = 0) -> None:
    """Settle the pending event if a paint followed its last work and the screen is quiet."""
    global _PENDING
    pending = _PENDING
    if pending is None or screen is not screen.app.screen:
        return
    why = pending["why"]
    if pending["t_paint"] <= pending["t_work"]:
        why["no paint after work"] = why.get("no paint after work", 0) + 1
        return
    reason = _not_settled(screen, own)
    if reason:
        why[reason] = why.get(reason, 0) + 1
        # Painted but not quiet yet (work queued on another node, a worker
        # running): look again in 2 ms on the raw event loop. A Textual timer
        # would count as pending work itself.
        if not pending.get("recheck"):
            pending["recheck"] = True

            def _again() -> None:
                if _PENDING is pending:
                    pending["recheck"] = False
                    try:
                        _check(screen)
                    except Exception:
                        pass

            import asyncio

            asyncio.get_running_loop().call_later(0.002, _again)
        return
    _emit({**_report(pending, time.perf_counter()), "status": "settled"})
    _PENDING = None


def _install() -> None:
    from textual import events
    from textual.app import App
    from textual.message_pump import MessagePump
    from textual.screen import Screen
    from textual.widgets import OptionList
    from textual.worker import Worker, WorkerState

    original_dispatch = MessagePump._dispatch_message

    async def _dispatch_message(self, message):
        key = id(self)
        _IN_FLIGHT[key] = _IN_FLIGHT.get(key, 0) + 1
        try:
            return await original_dispatch(self, message)
        finally:
            left = _IN_FLIGHT.get(key, 1) - 1
            if left:
                _IN_FLIGHT[key] = left
            else:
                _IN_FLIGHT.pop(key, None)

    MessagePump._dispatch_message = _dispatch_message

    original_on_event = App.on_event

    async def on_event(self, event):
        try:
            if type(self.screen).__name__ == "PersonasScreen":
                if isinstance(event, events.Key) and not event.is_forwarded:
                    _patch_pane()
                    _start(f"key:{event.key}")
                elif isinstance(event, events.Resize):
                    _patch_pane()
                    _start(f"resize:{event.size.width}x{event.size.height}")
        except Exception:
            pass
        return await original_on_event(self, event)

    App.on_event = on_event

    original_display = App._display

    def _display(self, screen, renderable):
        result = original_display(self, screen, renderable)
        try:
            if _PENDING is not None and renderable is not None and not self._batch_count:
                _PENDING["t_paint"] = time.perf_counter()
                _PENDING["paints"] += 1
                # The paint ran in the screen's update-timer task, not its message
                # queue, so no Idle follows it by itself: ask the screen to check
                # once it has processed what is queued.
                current = self.screen
                current.call_later(_check_safely, current, 1)
        except Exception:
            pass
        return result

    App._display = _display

    original_set_options = OptionList.set_options

    def set_options(self, *args, **kwargs):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        try:
            return original_set_options(self, *args, **kwargs)
        finally:
            if self.id == "personas-library-rows" and _PENDING is not None:
                _PENDING["set_options_ms"].append(round((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000, 2))
                _work_done()

    OptionList.set_options = set_options

    state_property = Worker.state

    def _set_state(self, state):
        state_property.fset(self, state)
        try:
            if state in (WorkerState.SUCCESS, WorkerState.ERROR, WorkerState.CANCELLED):
                if _owned_by(self._node, self._node.app.screen):
                    _work_done()
        except Exception:
            pass

    Worker.state = property(state_property.fget, _set_state)

    def _check_safely(screen, own: int = 0) -> None:
        try:
            _check(screen, own)
        except Exception:
            pass

    original_idle = Screen._on_idle

    async def _on_idle(self, event):
        await original_idle(self, event)
        try:
            _check(self)
        except Exception:
            pass

    Screen._on_idle = _on_idle


try:
    _install()
except Exception as exc:  # never stop the app
    _emit({"label": "install-failed", "error": repr(exc)})
EOF
cat > "$L/seed_5000.py" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""B2a live evidence: top a copy of the harness's `volume` master up to 5,000 characters.

Run ONLY through the harness's seedrun.sh, against the `volume5000` master
(spec 5.7.5: "a 5,000-character copy for B2a's latency evidence"):
  seedrun.sh "$HARNESS_STATE/volume5000" seed_5000.py
harness_guard (imported from the harness directory under APP_WT) refuses any
other profile, the real profile and every protected master. Cards go through
the app's own API (CharactersRAGDB.add_character_card) in one transaction.
"""

import os
import sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
sys.path.insert(
    0,
    os.path.join(
        os.environ["APP_WT"],
        "Docs/superpowers/qa/roleplay-library-layout-review-2026-10-01/harness",
    ),
)
import harness_guard  # noqa: E402

PROFILE = harness_guard.require_profile(allow_runs=False, allow_masters=("volume5000",))

from tldw_chatbook import config  # noqa: E402

harness_guard.check_app_paths(config, PROFILE)
db = config.get_chachanotes_db_lazy()
assert db is not None, "chachanotes db failed to open"
TARGET = 5000
before = db.count_character_cards()
TAGS = ("fantasy", "sci-fi", "noir", "mystery", "companion")
with db.transaction():
    for index in range(before, TARGET):
        db.add_character_card(
            {
                "name": f"Volume Character {index:04d}",
                "description": f"Seeded latency-evidence character number {index}.",
                "tags": [TAGS[index % len(TAGS)]],
            }
        )
after = db.count_character_cards()
print(f"characters: {before} -> {after}")
assert after == TARGET, after
EOF
cat > "$L/live_timing.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# B2a live timing, one cold run (AC#9, AC#10; evidence, never a pytest threshold).
# Usage: live_timing.sh <base|head> <master: volume|volume5000> <run-label>
# Boots the arm's app on a copy of <master> at 120x36 with the timing hooks
# (inject/sitecustomize.py through EXTRA_PYTHONPATH), opens Roleplay, then sends
# the measured events with a pause after each, so each one settles alone:
#   ctrl+f; search "a", "l" (two debounced search keystrokes); backspace x2;
#   escape (into the list); down x3; end (load-through at 5,000: every window);
#   home; end (every row resident); resize 120x36 -> 160x45 -> 120x36.
# Writes $OUT/<arm>-<master>-<run-label>.jsonl (one line per event).
set -u
ARM=$1; MASTER=$2; RUN=$3
MAIN=/Users/macbook-dev/Documents/GitHub/tldw_chatbook
LIVE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd -P)
: "${HARNESS_STATE:?set HARNESS_STATE}" "${OUT:?set OUT}" "${HEAD_WT:?set HEAD_WT}" "${BASE_WT:?set BASE_WT}"
case "$ARM" in
  base) export APP_WT=$BASE_WT ;;
  head) export APP_WT=$HEAD_WT ;;
  *) echo "usage: live_timing.sh <base|head> <master> <run-label>" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
H=$HEAD_WT/Docs/superpowers/qa/roleplay-library-layout-review-2026-10-01/harness
export EXTRA_PYTHONPATH=$LIVE/inject EXTRA_TOML=""
S="b2at${ARM:0:1}${RUN}"
PY=$MAIN/.venv/bin/python
key() { tmux -L "$S" send-keys "$@"; }
typ() { tmux -L "$S" send-keys -l "$1"; }
quit() {
  local pid i
  pid=$(tmux -L "$S" list-panes -a -F '#{pane_pid}' 2>/dev/null | head -1)
  tmux -L "$S" send-keys C-q 2>/dev/null || true
  for i in $(seq 1 300); do [ -n "$pid" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.1; done
  tmux -L "$S" kill-server 2>/dev/null || true
  # kill-server leaves the socket file behind; remove ours once no server answers on it
  tmux -L "$S" has-session 2>/dev/null || rm -f "${TMUX_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tmux-$(id -u)/$S"
}
"$H/launch.sh" "$S" 120 36 "$MASTER" > /dev/null || exit 1
RUNDIR=$HARNESS_STATE/runs/$S
if ! { "$PY" -B "$H/waitfor.py" "$S" "4 Roleplay" 240 > /dev/null && "$PY" -B "$H/waitfor.py" "$S" "Ctrl+Q" 30 > /dev/null; }; then
  echo "  !! boot timed out ($ARM $MASTER $RUN)"; quit; exit 1
fi
sleep 3
"$PY" -B "$H/where.py" "$S" "⌃4 Roleplay" --click > /dev/null
if ! "$PY" -B "$H/waitfor.py" "$S" "Modes:" 60 > /dev/null; then
  echo "  !! Roleplay never arrived ($ARM $MASTER $RUN)"; quit; exit 1
fi
sleep 8
key C-f; sleep 2.5
typ a; sleep 2.5
typ l; sleep 2.5
key BSpace; sleep 2.5
key BSpace; sleep 2.5
key Escape; sleep 2.5
key Down; sleep 1.5
key Down; sleep 1.5
key Down; sleep 1.5
key End; sleep 10
key Home; sleep 2.5
key End; sleep 2.5
tmux -L "$S" resize-window -x 160 -y 45; sleep 3
tmux -L "$S" resize-window -x 120 -y 36; sleep 3
quit
mkdir -p "$OUT"
if [ -f "$RUNDIR/home/b2a-timing.jsonl" ]; then
  cp "$RUNDIR/home/b2a-timing.jsonl" "$OUT/$ARM-$MASTER-$RUN.jsonl"
  echo "  $ARM $MASTER $RUN: $(wc -l < "$OUT/$ARM-$MASTER-$RUN.jsonl" | tr -d ' ') events"
else
  echo "  !! no timing file ($ARM $MASTER $RUN): the hooks did not load"
fi
EOF
cat > "$L/run_abba.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# B2a live timing: 10 cold runs per arm per profile, ABBA-interleaved (base head head base, x5),
# 348 characters (volume) first, then 5,000 (volume5000). Each run is live_timing.sh.
# Env: HARNESS_STATE, OUT, HEAD_WT, BASE_WT (as live_timing.sh). A failed run is retried once
# under a new label; its first attempt is listed in $OUT/failed-runs.txt.
set -u
LIVE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd -P)
mkdir -p "$OUT"
: > "$OUT/failed-runs.txt"
for MASTER in volume volume5000; do
  N=0
  for CYCLE in 1 2 3 4 5; do
    for ARM in base head head base; do
      N=$((N + 1))
      LABEL="${MASTER#volume}c${CYCLE}r${N}"
      LABEL=${LABEL:-c${CYCLE}r${N}}
      if ! bash "$LIVE/live_timing.sh" "$ARM" "$MASTER" "$LABEL" || [ ! -s "$OUT/$ARM-$MASTER-$LABEL.jsonl" ]; then
        echo "$ARM $MASTER $LABEL" >> "$OUT/failed-runs.txt"
        rm -f "$OUT/$ARM-$MASTER-$LABEL.jsonl"
        bash "$LIVE/live_timing.sh" "$ARM" "$MASTER" "${LABEL}x"
      fi
    done
  done
done
echo "runs: $(ls "$OUT"/*.jsonl | wc -l | tr -d ' ') ; failed first attempts: $(wc -l < "$OUT/failed-runs.txt" | tr -d ' ')"
EOF
cat > "$L/live_timing_summary.py" <<'EOF'
"""B2a live timing summary (AC#9, AC#10): medians over the ABBA runs, per arm, profile and event class.

Usage: live_timing_summary.py <dir of <arm>-<master>-<run>.jsonl files>

Per run, each class's value is the median of that run's settled events of the
class; the line reports the median and the 90th percentile of those per-run
values over every run of the arm. The 250 ms target and set_options <= 50 ms
apply to head (AC#9); the base arm is the comparison.
"""

import json
import statistics
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

CLASSES = {
    "search keystroke": lambda label, i: label in ("key:a", "key:l", "key:backspace"),
    "cursor key (down)": lambda label, i: label == "key:down",
    "end (load-through)": lambda label, i: label == "key:end" and i == 0,
    "end (rows resident)": lambda label, i: label == "key:end" and i == 1,
    "resize 120<->160": lambda label, i: label.startswith("resize:"),
}
per_run: dict[tuple[str, str, str], list[float]] = defaultdict(list)
set_options: dict[tuple[str, str], list[float]] = defaultdict(list)
for path in sorted(Path(sys.argv[1]).glob("*.jsonl")):
    arm, master, _run = path.stem.split("-", 2)
    events = [json.loads(line) for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip()]
    settled = [event for event in events if event.get("status") == "settled"]
    seen: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    values: dict[str, list[float]] = defaultdict(list)
    for event in settled:
        label = event["label"]
        index = seen[label]
        seen[label] += 1
        for name, match in CLASSES.items():
            if match(label, index):
                values[name].append(event["ms"])
                if name == "search keystroke" and event["set_options_ms"]:
                    set_options[(arm, master)].append(max(event["set_options_ms"]))
    for name, samples in values.items():
        per_run[(arm, master, name)].append(statistics.median(samples))


def describe(samples: list[float]) -> str:
    if not samples:
        return "n=0"
    ordered = sorted(samples)
    p90 = ordered[min(len(ordered) - 1, int(len(ordered) * 0.9))]
    return f"n={len(samples)} median {statistics.median(samples):.1f} ms (p90 {p90:.1f})"


for master in sorted({key[1] for key in per_run}):
    for name in CLASSES:
        base = per_run.get(("base", master, name), [])
        head = per_run.get(("head", master, name), [])
        verdict = "ok" if head and statistics.median(head) <= 250 else ("OVER" if head else "MISSING")
        print(f"live {master} {name}: base {describe(base)} | head {describe(head)} | head <= 250 ms: {verdict}")
    head_set = set_options.get(("head", master), [])
    if head_set:
        verdict = "ok" if statistics.median(head_set) <= 50 else "OVER"
        print(f"live {master} set_options per search keystroke: head {describe(head_set)} | <= 50 ms: {verdict}")
EOF
chmod +x "$L/live_timing.sh" "$L/run_abba.sh"
"$MAIN/.venv/bin/ruff" check "$L/inject/sitecustomize.py" "$L/seed_5000.py" "$L/live_timing_summary.py" | tail -1
OUTER
```

The gate: every `head <= 250 ms` verdict `ok` and the `set_options` verdict `ok` (AC#9; AC#10's two rows are the End with rows resident and the resize at `volume5000`). ```bash

cat > "$EV/gates/pr_body.py" <<'EOF'
"""Write the B2a PR body from the evidence (never typed numbers).

Usage: pr_body.py <EV> <base worktree> <head worktree>  > pr-body.md

Reads EV/gates/gates.txt (the lines Task 13 Steps 2-8 append), EV/preimport-{base,head}.json (Task 0's measurement),
EV/mutations.md, EV/owner-answers.txt, EV/owner-decisions.txt (Task 0 Step 6), EV/base-sha.txt and
EV/gates/unproven.txt (optional), and
both arms' ratchet, broad-selector and pre-import files. A value it cannot find prints as MISSING.
"""

import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ev, base_wt, head_wt = (Path(arg) for arg in sys.argv[1:4])
gates = (ev / "gates" / "gates.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
RATCHET = "Tests/Architecture/test_module_size_ratchet.py"
FASTPATH = "Tests/Performance/test_textual_css_fastpath.py"
PREIMPORT = "Tests/Performance/test_screen_preimport_payload_budget.py"
PS = "tldw_chatbook/UI/Screens/personas_screen.py"
PLP = "tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Persona_Widgets/personas_library_pane.py"
FS = "tldw_chatbook/UI/Persona_Modules/roleplay_frame_state.py"


def last(prefix: str) -> str:
    """The last gates.txt line that starts with prefix (later measurements win)."""
    found = [line for line in gates if line.startswith(prefix)]
    return found[-1] if found else "MISSING"


def field(arm: str, name: str) -> str:
    match = re.search(rf"\b{name}=([^ |]+)", last(f"{arm} | "))
    return match[1] if match else "MISSING"


def num(text: str) -> str:
    return f"{int(text):,}" if text.isdigit() else text


def delta(name: str) -> str:
    b, h = field("base", name), field("head", name)
    return f"{int(h) - int(b):+,}" if b.isdigit() and h.isdigit() else "MISSING"


def ratchet_row(root: Path, rel: str) -> str:
    match = re.search(rf'^    "{re.escape(rel)}": (\d+),$', (root / RATCHET).read_text(encoding="utf-8"), re.M)
    return f"{int(match[1]):,}" if match else "none"


def constant(root: Path, rel: str, name: str) -> str:
    match = re.search(rf"^{name} = ([\d_]+)$", (root / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8"), re.M)
    return f"{int(match[1].replace('_', '')):,}" if match else "MISSING"


def lines_of(root: Path, rel: str) -> str:
    path = root / rel
    return f"{len(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines()):,}" if path.exists() else "absent"


def block(pattern: str) -> list[str]:
    return [line for line in gates if re.match(pattern, line)]


pre = {arm: json.loads((ev / f"preimport-{arm}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) for arm in ("base", "head")}
base_sha = (ev / "base-sha.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()[:10]

w("### What changed")
w("- **The list.** Roleplay's paged `ListView` (one mounted widget per row, 50 rows a page) becomes `RoleplayItemList`, an `OptionList` that keeps the id `#personas-library-rows` and reads the database in windows of 200 rows (`add_options`), with the spec 1.5.6 safety rules: duplicate ids dropped and logged, never raised; a window fence, so a late window from a superseded query is dropped; writes reload from the anchor; load-through to a target row. Prompts are literal `Content` (markup is never parsed), one or two lines per item by width and count, a 3-cell gutter (`▸` loaded, `✓` marked; `>` and `[x]` in ASCII mode), middle-ellipsised names with the whole name in a hover tooltip, relative ages. Width-independent prompts are never rebuilt and the others once per settled width.")
w("- **Counts in the border.** The list's top border names the kind and its count (`Characters 349`, `… 48 of 349 · tag fantasy`, `(…)` while counting, `100+` on a server until known, `(?)` on failure); the bottom border gives the open item's `#N of M`. The pager and the count line are gone.")
w("- **Marks, the marks bar and one delete modal (R32).** Marks are kept by id and per kind, survive search, sort, tags and kind switches, and are cleared on leaving Roleplay (never saved, R16). While marks exist the pane's bottom row is the marks bar (`✓ 3 marked (2 hidden) · Export… · Delete… · Clear esc`). Every delete asks once, in the same dialog: the Inspector's Delete names the open item; the marks bar's `Delete…` lists up to five names and `and N more`, and its button reads `Delete N marked`. `m`, `Space` (lore books and dictionaries, with a `… turned off · space to undo` toast) and `s` act on the list only.")
w("- **The visit-lifecycle leave hook (§4.11):** on leave (unmount or `ScreenSuspend`) the marks clear and the window worker is cancelled, and a resume starts none; a modal over Roleplay keeps the marks.")
w("- **CSS:** the `ListView`'s rules leave (boot and `BUNDLED_CSS`); the focus edge is box-stable (a left border column present at rest and on focus, only its colour changes), so a click on an unfocused list lands on the row under the pointer; the broad-selector ratchet is lowered to the measurement.")

- [ ] **Step 2: The follow-ups: an id sweep across every remote and worktree, then the files**

Task ids collide when two sessions mint from the same observed maximum (`backlog/docs/lessons-backlog-hygiene.md`: "Task IDs collide constantly — sweep every remote, not just dev", and its 2026-08-21 tie-break: the older arrival keeps an id). This block sweeps both namespaces this task mints in, the Roleplay-frame children (`task-33910.N`) and the top-level ids, over every object reachable from every ref and over every worktree's files; takes the child maximum + 1 and the top-level maximum + 20 (headroom against a concurrent session minting from the same maximum); then checks each candidate as a content reference on dev and on every remote branch not yet merged into dev (open PRs' branches among them), where a task can be cited before its file lands, moving past any hit; and records the two ids:

```bash
bash <<'EOF'
set -u
MAIN=/Users/macbook-dev/Documents/GitHub/tldw_chatbook; EV=$MAIN/.worktrees/.b2a-evidence
git -C "$MAIN" fetch --all --prune --quiet
WTS=$(git -C "$MAIN" worktree list --porcelain | sed -n 's/^worktree //p' | while read -r W; do ls "$W/backlog/tasks" 2>/dev/null; done)
C_REFS=$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-list --objects --all | grep -oE 'task-33910\.[0-9]+' | cut -d. -f2 | sort -n | tail -1)
C_WTS=$(echo "$WTS" | grep -oE 'task-33910\.[0-9]+' | cut -d. -f2 | sort -n | tail -1)
T_REFS=$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-list --objects --all | grep -oE 'task-[0-9]+' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | sort -n | tail -1)
T_WTS=$(echo "$WTS" | grep -oE '^task-[0-9]+' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | sort -n | tail -1)
echo "TASK-33910 children: max $C_REFS in every ref, $C_WTS in every worktree; top-level: max $T_REFS in every ref, $T_WTS in every worktree"
N=$(( (C_REFS > C_WTS ? C_REFS : C_WTS) + 1 )); M=$(( (T_REFS > T_WTS ? T_REFS : T_WTS) + 20 ))
REFS="origin/dev $(git -C "$MAIN" for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' --no-merged origin/dev refs/remotes/ | tr '\n' ' ')"
hits() { git -C "$MAIN" grep -l -i -F -w "$1" $REFS -- backlog Docs/superpowers 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '; }
while [ "$(hits "task-33910.$N")" != 0 ]; do N=$((N + 1)); done
while [ "$(hits "task-$M")" != 0 ]; do M=$((M + 1)); done
echo "$N $M" > "$EV/followup-ids.txt"
echo "follow-up ids: TASK-33910.$N and TASK-$M (no content reference on dev or any unmerged remote branch)"
EOF
```

The whole block took 2 m 36 s, most of it the two `git grep` calls over dev and 104 unmerged remote branches. Run after a test filing of `task-33910.31` in a scratch worktree, it read `31 in every worktree` and chose `TASK-33910.32 and TASK-36034`: the worktree half of the sweep is what catches an id minted on a branch nobody pushed.
